deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 154, 1983-84): Grothendieck is studying finite systems of pseudo-lines X in a topological projective plane. He considers positions of an additional pseudo-line D relative to X: 'stable' pseudo-lines (general position), transitions and specializations between them, and singular positions where two candidates D, D' 'superpose' along a common segment ('positions superposi-singulières'). On the previous page he builds a surface 𝒳 with an immersion φ: 𝒳 → X and a topological graph K, whose faces correspond to stable pseudo-lines. Each face is a disc Δ*_D attached to a stable D. These discs are glued along arcs a, b, either by 'parallel transport' or by the opposite identification. He checks how orientations ω_F, ω_D are transported. With one choice the circuits around superposi-singular positions come out right.

This page. (1) The general 'circuits', meaning closed paths in the transition graph other than the small loops around superposi-singular positions, remain mysterious to him; he does not know whether they are 'bitables' (reading uncertain).

(2) The two gluing choices correspond to the polygonal structure given by one of the 'quantisations' (= transitions) of a stable D. There is a second polygonal structure: certain transition arcs on \tilde D are naturally disjoint. One can therefore use the polygonal structure they define in the topological realization in which D is 'linear'. The trouble is that a polygon of order n (rather than 2n) does not clearly correspond to an n-gonal disc. He suggests this may be a way to obtain both types at once, using disjoint copies of the discs Δ*_{\hat D}, Δ*_{\hat D'}, perhaps producing Möbius bands.

(3) Right column, new idea. Figure: two pseudo-lines D (green) and D' (yellow) coincide outside a bigon. Inside the bigon a dotted 'common part' runs, crossed by two lines of X (red X). He proposes to cut the X along the common part of D and D'. The local picture sits inside a Möbius band, in which parallel lines become a rectangular band. Orientations should perhaps be 'twisted by ω(D)'. The Möbius bands (of 'order 2') are made of two rectangles glued along two pairs of edges. If he is not mistaken, this amounts to identifying, simultaneously and via parallel transport, \hat a with b and \hat a' with b'.

(4) The question he ends on: when all these gluings of all the Δ*_D are carried out, is the result exactly the cellular surface determined by the graph Γ_D with its polygonal structure and transport data? The next page continues this into a combinatorial description. Vertices are the stable pseudo-lines. Oriented edges are pairs (D, a) with a a transition arc (a specialization or its antipode). The polygons come from the transition arcs, and the surface 𝒳 carries an involution over X.

Purpose: to give a combinatorial cell-complex (surface) model of the space of positions of one extra pseudo-line relative to a given arrangement, with an antipodal involution. In modern terms this is the space of single-element extensions of the rank-3 oriented matroid of X, and to understand its circuits (its fundamental group / connectivity).
errors: No outright error. The page is explicitly tentative ('Sauf erreur', 'non ??', 'peut-être').

Two rectangles glued along two pairs of edges give a Möbius band only with an odd total twist; with an even twist they give an annulus. Which one occurs depends on the orientation convention, and that is precisely what he flags as unclear ('twisté par ω(D) ?').
On the left side he admits a gap: an n-gon (rather than a 2n-gon) does not obviously bound an n-gonal disc in the second polygonal structure. This is unresolved.

ideas.what: Building a surface from discs Δ*_D, one per stable pseudo-line D added to an arrangement X, glued along transition arcs by parallel transport. The surface carries an antipodal involution and an immersion to X, and its faces correspond to stable positions.
ideas.modern_name: Extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid (space of single-element extensions / pseudo-line extensions of an arrangement), or a dual cell model of it
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sturmfels & Ziegler, 'Extension spaces of oriented matroids' (1993); Mnëv & Ziegler (1993) for higher-rank counterexamples. The background is Goodman–Pollack, Las Vergnas and Bland–Las Vergnas on pseudo-line arrangements and oriented matroids.
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA. Possibly alluded to in Récoltes et Semailles or other late writings on pseudo-lines; unsure.

ideas.what: Checking how orientations of discs and of pseudo-lines are transported along transition arcs. The two possible gluings (parallel transport or its opposite) give opposite answers, and twisting by ω(D) is considered.
ideas.modern_name: Orientation local system / orientation double cover on a cell complex; sign conventions for flips

ideas.what: Local model near a superposi-singular position (D and D' share a segment crossed by lines of X): cut along the common part, observe that the gluing lives in a Möbius band built from two rectangles, and identify \hat a with b and \hat a' with b' simultaneously.
ideas.modern_name: Local structure of the extension space near a degenerate (non-generic) extension; flip/mutation loops
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in oriented matroid literature (mutations, Ringel flips; Sturmfels–Ziegler)

ideas.what: Question whether 'more general circuits' in the transition graph are generated by the elementary circuits around superposi-singular positions.
ideas.modern_name: Simple connectivity / presentation of the fundamental groupoid of the extension space (2-cells generated by local flip relations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sturmfels–Ziegler (rank 3 extension spaces are homotopy-equivalent to S^2)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's surface 𝒳 has these features: faces indexed by stable positions of an extra pseudo-line, an involution, and an immersion over the projective plane X. This appears to be an independent 1983-84 construction of what became the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid. His worry about general circuits is the question of whether this space is a 2-sphere (simply connected), settled affirmatively in rank 3 by Sturmfels–Ziegler only in 1993. The notes thus anticipate the extension-space problem from the topological, 'tame-topology' side.
missed.quote: Mais les circuits plus généraux restent mystérieux pour moi ... de tous les Δ*_D est-ce bien la surface cellulaire obtenue par le groupe Γ_D et sa structure de polygonalisation et de transport ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly of historical interest: an early, independent formulation of the extension-space question. The explicit Möbius-band / parallel-transport local gluing rule could offer a different, more geometric proof viewpoint, but no new theorem is evident.

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes a second polygonal structure, from naturally disjoint transition arcs, giving n-gons instead of 2n-gons. He also proposes obtaining both cell structures 'simultaneously' via Möbius bands. Both are left unresolved.
missed.quote: peut-être est-ce une indication pour obtenir simultanément les deux types ... de façon à obtenir des rubans de Möbius peut-être ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would amount to a pair of dual or subdivided cell structures on the extension space. It is a small, likely routine thread.

deep.surprise_reason: This is exploratory, tentative work on cell structures for the space of positions of a pseudo-line relative to an arrangement. It is interesting historically as an apparently independent anticipation of oriented-matroid extension spaces (later Sturmfels–Ziegler), but the page contains no finished result absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'p.v. stable D' is very likely 'p.d. stable D' (pseudo-droite), consistent with the next page.
'dite à superpositions géométriques' may read 'dû à n superpositions géométriques'; uncertain.
'l'identification en simultané de â avec b, â' avec b'': the second identification is written with a struck-out symbol corrected to â' (or a'), not â again.
'se donne dans un ruban de Möbius' plausibly 'se trouve dans un ruban de Möbius'.
'Mais ce qu'il est vrai' likely 'Mais est-il vrai que'; 'est celle bien' likely 'est-ce bien'.
'obtenue par le groupe Γ_D' could be 'graphe Γ_D', matching the next page's 'graphe Γ'.
